text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated error rate and routing oscillation on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 -> observed cross-region fallback loop to us-east-1. Paging oncall.

maria: ack, stepping in. oncall handover — I'm on it. what do we know so far?

ajay: full context: we deployed a schema change to routing policies ~09:12 UTC that deprecated `prefer_variant` in favor of `variant_selector`. migration was supposed to map missing fields to explicit default, but looks like omitted fields are being treated as `prefer_variant: legacy` in the new parser.

lee: seeing the same — spiky 5xxs starting ~09:18; traces show repeated reroutes: eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 for the same request id, TTL on KV cache gets invalidated causing repeated cold starts.

carla: customer impact: about 3% of production traffic hitting /v1/generate in eu region showing >1200ms p95 and a doubled error count for last 20m. a few large customers reported degraded response times.

maria: prioritize mitigation: can we pin a safe variant or force single-region routing while we debug? we don't want oscillation to keep happening.

ajay: yes, recommend forcing route to `baseline-alpha-2025` variant that is in all regions. quick API patch:

```
# force variant via control plane
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routing/policies/force \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"selector":"service:inference","force_variant":"baseline-alpha-2025","scope":"eu-west-1"}'
```

sam: I'll run that now and keep watchers on latency. giving a heads-up to infra to hold any more schema rollouts.

ops-bot: action executed by sam at 09:27 UTC: applied forced-variant policy to eu-west-1 for service:inference. watchers deployed.

lee: after force, immediate reduction in oscillation traces. 5xxs dropping, p95 back down to ~350ms. still seeing some backlog but healthy trend. :thumbsup:

carla: logging note for customers: who to notify? ops-team suggested notifying top 5 affected customers and offering optional migration guidance.

maria: good. ajay, can you confirm root cause hypothesis: the schema mapper treats missing `variant_selector` as `prefer_variant=legacy`? if so, we need a hotfix mapping to default to explicit baseline.

ajay: yep reproducer: local mapper accepts the new schema, but the fallback branch was left to preserve legacy behavior. sample snippet:

```
# faulty mapping
if (routing.prefer_variant == undefined) {
  // legacy fallback left in accidentally
  routing.prefer_variant = 'legacy';
}

# intended mapping
// should map missing to baseline-explicit
```

maria: that explains why some customers suddenly matched legacy-only variants that have capacity constraints -> causing cross-region spill and oscillation.

sam: timeline: roll forward patch to mapper to map missing -> baseline-explicit. but we should prefer rollback of the schema deploy (it touched multiple services). recommendations?

lee: quick path: 1) keep forced-variant applied 2) push a tiny hotfix to mapper that changes default to `baseline-explicit` and bundle unit test 3) schedule full rollback if hotfix is risky.

ajay: i'll prep the hotfix PR now. small change, test added. CI should be quick; can merge with emergency flag if SRE approves.

carla: Customer ops: drafted a short message for affected customers explaining degraded perf and mitigation. still need legal review for wording (no PII). pinging comms.

ops-bot: alert: external incident page created: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3971122334

maria: two operational asks: (1) hold on schema rollouts until postmortem, (2) create a rollback playbook for routing schema mappings. tagging infra and releases.

ajay: PR up as draft at https://git.internal/routing/merge_requests/4022 - small change. requesting expedited review from lee and sam.

lee: reviewing now. tests look good. running staging deploy.

sam: staging run shows mapping now defaults to baseline, no regressions. staging smoke passes.

ops-bot: staging -> canary deploy started at 09:44 UTC.

maria: once canary looks green, we'll merge and roll to prod with 5m canaries. keep forced-variant active until rollout completes.

lee: canary healthy. merging.

ops-bot: prod rollout started 09:52 UTC, incremental 10% steps. monitoring performance and reroute logs.

carla: current impact: error rate back to baseline, customers still seeing occasional >500ms due to backlog but trending down. flagged top customers notified by comms.

maria: great. post-incident actions: 
- disable implicit legacy fallback in schema parser permanently
- add unit + integration tests for mapping behavior
- add a `router` healthcheck that detects oscillating reroutes per-request
- update runbook to include forced-variant step

ajay: noted. I'll add tests and a follow-up MR for runbook edits.

sam: leaving forced-variant in place for 1 hour post-rollout to be safe, then will remove if metrics stable.

ops-bot: forced-variant removed by sam at 10:22 UTC.

lee: removing forced-variant didn't reintroduce oscillation. metrics stable for 30m.

maria: incident declared resolved at 10:40 UTC. follow-up postmortem to be scheduled for tomorrow with infra, product, and engineering leads.

carla: logging impact summary for postmortem: ~3% of traffic in eu-west-1 affected for ~22m window, peak error spike 6.8% for 3m, customers notified.

ajay: postmortem items assigned in tracker. will include patch link and test coverage.

maria: thanks all. nice coordinated response. closing thread here; please append any additional notes to the postmortem doc.
